messages:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty ALERT P3052 -> GPU queue growth on generation-prod. Queue length > 1200, median wait > 45s, paging Nate (oncall).
Nate: acknowledged. I'm on it. starting triage. linking cluster and autoscaler logs.
Alex: seeing a big backlog in the generation namespace, ~420 pending pods with reason: "0/60 nodes are available: 60 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector/affinity, 120 Insufficient memory, 300 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu".
Priya: cluster-autoscaler logs pulled. key errors: "Failed to scale up: launch template mismatch for nodegroup generation-gpu-ng-1" and repeated "AccessDenied: iam:PassRole" when trying to create instances.
Jamie: checking AWS ASG limits — the generation GPU ASG is at desired=4, max=4 (set by infra policy). Autoscaler requested scale but ASG refused due to max size.
Emily: so autoscaler requests bumped but ASG capped. Why launch template mismatch though?
Sasha: I pulled the launch template versions. The active LT for that nodegroup changed yesterday during a deploy: missing user-data fragment that adds the gpu taint and kubelet labels. New instances are coming up without the taint, kubelet labels, and nodeRole, so pods with nodeAffinity/taint tolerations can't be scheduled.
Nate: that explains pending pods and "didn't match" message: scheduler rejects nodes without required labels/taints.
Alex: also seeing cluster-autoscaler errors "scaleUp failed: cannot find compatible launch template version with required instance type: p4d. Some launch template versions list instance types not supported by GPU pool".
Priya: and the iam:PassRole error indicates the autoscaler role lost permission to pass the instance-profile role after a recent IRSA/role cleanup. Combine that with ASG max=4 and launch template mismatch -> scale up fails consistently.
Jamie: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase ASG max temporarily and manually set desired, 2) revert launch template to previous version that includes taint and user-data, 3) patch IAM to allow iam:PassRole, 4) enable CPU fallback routing for non-critical traffic.
Emily: prioritize quick customer impact reduction first. Jamie, can you manually set ASG desired to 8? I can revert LT in parallel.
Jamie: scaling ASG now: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name generation-gpu-asg --max-size 12 --desired-capacity 8` — running.
infra-bot: ASG update accepted (console job id asg-async-99). New instances launching.
Alex: starting traffic reroute plan: switching lower-priority routes to cpu-light model via router toggle so premium customers keep GPU until capacity stabilizes.
Alex: applying router config: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/toggle -d '{"route":"gen:cpu-fallback","state":"on","scope":"non-premium"}'` -> 200 OK.
CS-Ops: notifying impacted non-premium customers and posting status page note: "AI generation latency degraded for some customers; mitigation in progress".
Priya: reverting launch template: retrieving LT v23 which has gpu taint/user-data. applying `aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-0abcd --default-version 23`.
Sasha: new nodes from ASG are joining but kubelet not registering properly on two instances because user-data didn't run — these are instances still using the broken LT version cached by ASG. We need to force new instances to use the updated default version.
Jamie: terminating the two mis-configured instances so ASG launches fresh ones with correct LT v23. `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids i-0aaa i-0bbb`.
infra-bot: instances terminated. new instances booting; cloud-init logs show GPU drivers installing.
Alex: router metrics show traffic shifted, latency for non-premium back to normal, premium still slightly elevated but within SLO for short requests.
Nate: cluster-autoscaler now logs: "scaleUp: successfully scaled up" and nodes registering with labels `node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true` and taint `nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule` — pods with tolerations are scheduling.
Emily: iam:PassRole fix — Priya, confirm IAM change applied?
Priya: updated autoscaler role policy to include `iam:PassRole` for instance-profile role. Verified with `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` -> PASS.
Alex: generating post-impact summary for CS: impacted ~15% of long-running generation requests for 18 minutes; customers who hit the queue saw retries but no data loss. CS-Ops preparing email for affected customers.
CS-Ops: acknowledgement. scheduling status update to be sent in 30m with root-cause summary.
Jamie: leaving ASG max at 12 temporarily and adding autoscaler scaleUp timeout tweak to 10m to reduce flapping.
Sasha: proposed follow-ups: (1) add CI gate to launch template changes to ensure required tags/taints and user-data fragments are present; (2) add an alert if autoscaler IAM permissions change or if ASG is at max capacity for 5m with pending pods; (3) add automated verification that new nodes have expected taints/labels before accepting them for scheduling.
Emily: agree. I'm owning the postmortem and will coordinate with infra and platform to create action items. Owner: Emily. Timeline: draft in 48h, final in 7 days.
Nate: handing off oncall to Emily (taking over). Nate: shifting to watch-only.
incidents-bot: oncall handoff recorded: Nate -> Emily at 1789155620.
deploy-bot: noted deploys paused for generation-gpu nodegroup until postmortem completed.
Priya: leaving a short runbook note in infra docs: steps we took to remediate (ASG scale, LT rollback, terminate bad instances, IAM patch, router fallback).
Alex: I'll keep router fallback available as runway for 2h. re-enabling normal routing in 30m if metrics stable.
Emily: closing incident channel once CS note goes out and cluster metrics stable (pending pods < 10 for 10min and queue length < 50). Thanks team.
CS-Ops: alert subscribers updated, scheduled follow-ups with top 10 customers who reported latency.
Sasha: logging required artifacts for postmortem: autoscaler logs, ASG activity history, launch template versions, kubelet cloud-init logs, router toggles.
Emily: great. I'll file the P0 postmortem and assign action items. ending thread here and will post link to the doc when ready. :white_check_mark:
